source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 3, 31. Ἁρμόζει τοῦτο καὶ πρὸς τοὺς έν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ λέγοντας τὰ ἐν τῷ ἑβδομηκοστῷ τρίτῳ Ψαλμῷ· «ἱνατί, ὁ θεός, ἀπώσω εἰς τέλος; ὠργίσθη ὁ θυμός σου ἐπὶ πρόβατα νομῆς σου;« σύμφωνον δὲ τὸ «οὐκ εἰς τέλος ἀπώσεται κύριος οὐδὲ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μηνιεῖ«· ἐρεῖ δὲ τῷ πρὸς ἀξίαν μετανοήσαντι· «διαλειπέτω ἡ φωνή σου ἀπὸ κλαυθμοῦ, καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου ἀπὸ δακρύων.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] This also fits toward those in the captivity saying the things in the seventy-third Psalm: “why, O God, have you thrust away unto the end? has your wrath been angered upon sheep of your pasture?” And in concert is “the Lord will not thrust away unto the end, nor will he be wrathful unto the age”; and he will say to the one who has repented toward worth: “let your voice leave off from weeping, and your eyes from tears.”
pass_b_english: This also fits toward those in the captivity saying the things in the seventy-third Psalm: “why, O God, have you thrust away unto the end? has your wrath been angered upon sheep of your pasture?” And in concert is “the Lord will not thrust away unto the end, nor will he be wrathful unto the age”; and he will say to the one who has repented toward worth: “let your voice leave off from weeping, and your eyes from tears.”

choices.why: Origen’s reading of nephroi/arrows in Lam 3:13.
